# rag-ferrite — Hybrid RAG engine (Rust)

> Personal RAG engine — simple, fast, Rust. One binary (15 MB), one DB, native collections. MCP-native.

## What it does

Turns documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, HTML) into queryable knowledge with semantic understanding.
Single Rust binary, SQLite storage, multi-collection, hybrid search with LLM-powered intelligence.

## Quick start

```bash
# One-line install (Linux x86_64)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lelabdev/rag-ferrite/main/install.sh | bash

# Or build from source
git clone https://github.com/lelabdev/rag-ferrite.git
cd rag-ferrite && cargo build --release
```

Requires: `poppler-utils` for PDF, an LLM provider, an embedding provider.

## Configuration

```toml
# config.toml — minimal config
data_dir = "./data"

[embedding]
provider = "openai"                    # any OpenAI-compatible API
model = "qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b"
dimensions = 4096
base_url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

[llm]
provider = "ollama"                    # ollama, openai, openrouter
model = "gemma4:31b"
base_url = "https://api.ollama.com"
context_enabled = true                 # contextual retrieval
relevance_scoring = true               # filter junk at ingestion
min_relevance_score = 5.0              # 1-10, chunks below are discarded

[reranker]
reranker_type = "llm"                  # disabled, llm, or cohere
top_k = 10
preview_chars = 300
```

API keys via environment: `LLM_API_KEY`, `EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, or `.env` file.

## MCP Tools (9)

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `query_documents(query, collection?, limit?)` | Hybrid search with filters, reranking, expansion, cache |
| `ingest_file(file_path, collection?)` | Ingest PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD |
| `ingest_data(content, source, collection?, format?)` | Ingest raw text, HTML, or markdown |
| `delete_file(source)` | Remove document and all its chunks |
| `list_files()` | List indexed documents |
| `status()` | Engine status and document count |
| `read_chunk_neighbors(source_id, chunk_index)` | Expand context around a chunk |
| `check_ingestion(file_path?, content?, source_name?)` | Preview document quality before ingestion |
| `benchmark(file_path, collection?, limit?)` | Evaluate retrieval quality against a golden dataset |

## Ingestion Pipeline

```
Document → Extract text (pdftotext / docx-lite / raw)
         → Chunk (auto/recursive/parent-child, configurable)
         → Relevance scoring (LLM rates 1-10, filters junk)
         → Contextual retrieval (LLM adds context prefix to each chunk)
         → Auto-tagging (LLM generates 2-3 tags per chunk)
         → Embed batch → Store in SQLite + HNSW index + BM25
```

### What gets filtered at ingestion

- Tables of contents, index pages, boilerplate
- Chunks scoring below `min_relevance_score` (default: 5/10)
- Duplicates detected via content hashing
- Chunks too small to be meaningful (< 200 chars merged with previous)

### Ingestion quality check

Before ingesting, use `check_ingestion()` to preview:
- Character count, estimated chunk count
- Language detection
- Duplicate detection against existing documents
- Warnings for very large or very small documents

## Query Pipeline

```
Query → Classify (simple / standard / complex)
      → [standard/complex] Query expansion (LLM multi-query)
      → Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + HNSW + RRF fusion)
      → [standard/complex] LLM reranking (0-1 scoring of top results)
      → Query cache (TTL 300s in memory)
      → Quality gate (confidence score)
      → [low confidence] Corrective RAG (reformulate + retry)
      → Return top-k chunks with tags and scores
```

### Query classification

- **Simple**: direct keyword match (e.g. "what is X?")
- **Standard**: needs expansion + reranking (e.g. "compare X and Y")
- **Complex**: multi-step reasoning (e.g. "how does X relate to Y given Z?")

Classification is automatic. Each level activates more pipeline stages.

### Reranking options

- `disabled`: no reranking, fast
- `llm`: uses configured LLM to score results (0-1)
- `cohere`: Cohere Rerank API (configurable model and URL)

## Collections

Multi-collection in the same SQLite database. Each MCP tool accepts an optional `collection` parameter.
Collections are created on-the-fly — no setup needed.

Use cases: separate work docs from personal notes, per-project knowledge bases, language-based splits.

## Architecture

```
rag-ferrite (single binary, 15 MB)
├── MCP server (rmcp, stdio) — for Hermes, Claude Desktop, any MCP client
├── HTTP API (axum, optional) — REST endpoints for web dashboards
├── Embedding provider — OpenAI-compatible APIs, Ollama local models
├── LLM provider — Ollama, OpenAI, OpenRouter, any OpenAI-compatible
├── Reranker — LLM-based or Cohere
├── Chunker — recursive + parent-child, section-aware, markdown-aware
├── Extractor — PDF (pdftotext), DOCX (docx-lite), TXT, MD
└── Storage — SQLite + HNSW (persistent to disk) + BM25
```

### Source structure

```
src/
├── main.rs        — MCP server entry point
├── service.rs     — shared service layer (MCP + HTTP)
├── api.rs         — HTTP REST endpoints (axum)
├── pipeline.rs    — query orchestration, classification, cache
├── engine/
│   ├── mod.rs     — engine init, ingest_text, ingest_file
│   ├── search.rs  — hybrid search with RRF fusion
│   ├── query.rs   — list, delete, neighbors, sources
│   ├── benchmark.rs — quality evaluation
│   └── tags.rs    — chunk tagging
├── llm.rs         — LLM provider (Ollama + OpenAI), scoring, tagging, context
├── tag_rules.rs   — Tag normalization rules loaded from tag-rules.toml
├── reranker.rs    — reranker (LLM, Cohere, passthrough)
├── embedding.rs   — embedding provider (OpenAI-compatible)
├── config.rs      — TOML config parsing
├── chunker.rs     — recursive + parent-child chunking, section extraction, language detection
├── extractor.rs   — PDF/DOCX/text extraction
└── types.rs       — shared structs
```

## Advanced Configuration

### LLM tuning

```toml
[llm]
temperature = 0.3                # scoring/tagging consistency
max_tokens = 150                 # per LLM call
expansion_temperature = 0.7      # query expansion creativity
expansion_max_tokens = 200
max_expansion_queries = 4        # alternative queries per original
max_document_prompt_chars = 8000 # context window for prompts
max_chunk_prompt_chars = 2000
context_batch_size = 20          # parallel chunks during ingestion
max_concurrent = 3               # concurrent LLM calls
```

### Chunking

Three strategies via `[chunking]` config:

| Strategy | How | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `recursive` | Fixed-size chunks (~800 chars) with overlap | Short docs, notes, FAQ |
| `parent_child` | Large parents (~2000 chars) → small children (~200 chars). Children embedded for search, parents returned for context | Books, manuals, long-form |
| `auto` (default) | parent_child for docs ≥ 5000 chars, recursive for smaller | Mixed collections |

```toml
[chunking]
strategy = "auto"                    # recursive, parent_child, or auto
parent_max_chars = 2000              # parent chunk size (parent_child mode)
child_max_chars = 200                # child chunk size (parent_child mode)
child_overlap = 20                   # overlap between child chunks
auto_threshold = 5000                # switch to parent_child above this size
```

### Query pipeline

```toml
[advanced]
quality_threshold = 0.3           # minimum confidence to accept
max_retries = 1                   # corrective RAG retries
high_confidence_threshold = 0.7   # above = high confidence
query_limit = 10                  # default result count
```

### Database

```toml
[advanced]
db_pool_size = 4                  # SQLite connection pool
db_busy_timeout_ms = 5000
embedding_batch_size = 20         # embeddings per API call
# RAM optimization
defer_index_rebuild = true        # skip HNSW rebuild after each file, flush once at end
wal_checkpoint_interval = 50      # WAL checkpoint every N children committed
```

### Tag rules (`tag-rules.toml`)

Auto-generated tags are cleaned through a configurable pipeline. Create `tag-rules.toml` alongside `config.toml`:

```toml
[synonyms]
"advertising" = "copywriting"
"social media" = "social media strategy"
"props" = "svelte"

[stop_words]
words = ["creative", "general", "basic", "success", "example"]
meta = ["introduction", "conclusion", "references", "glossary"]
technical = ["syntax", "configuration", "installation", "deployment"]
emotional = ["fear", "stress", "passion", "ambition"]
noise = ["anecdote", "humor", "placeholder", "guide", "tutorial"]

[rules]
min_length = 3           # minimum tag length in characters
max_words = 3            # maximum words per tag
strip_chars = "*$`\"<>|={}[]/"  # characters removed before processing
```

**Pipeline:** strip chars → lowercase → synonym lookup → stop word filter → length filter → singular normalization → dedup.

No recompilation needed — edit the file and restart the service.

### Reranker (Cohere)

```toml
[reranker]
reranker_type = "cohere"
model = "rerank-v3.5"                          # optional, defaults to rerank-v3.5
base_url = "https://api.cohere.ai/v2/rerank"   # optional, defaults to Cohere API
api_key = "your-cohere-api-key"                 # or set COHERE_API_KEY env var
top_k = 10
preview_chars = 300
```

### Logging and HTTP

```toml
[advanced]
log_file = "rag-ferrite.log"
log_filter = "rag_ferrite=debug,rag_engine=debug"
http_bind_address = "0.0.0.0"    # for REST API (if http_port > 0)
```

## Hermes / MCP Client Setup

### Option A — stdio (local, simple)

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  rag-ferrite:
    command: /path/to/rag-ferrite
    timeout: 9999        # large files can take 10+ min with contextual retrieval
    env:
      LLM_API_KEY: "..."
      EMBEDDING_API_KEY: "..."
```

### Option B — Streamable HTTP (recommended for production / remote)

Set `http_port = 4242` in config.toml. rag-ferrite serves MCP over HTTP at `/mcp`.

```yaml
# Hermes — local or remote
mcp_servers:
  rag-ferrite:
    url: "http://localhost:4242/mcp"
    timeout: 9999
```

**Why Streamable HTTP:**
- Independent service — survives client restarts
- Works over the network — run on any server
- Multiple clients can connect
- Long ingestions decoupled from client lifecycle

### Claude Desktop / any MCP client

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "rag-ferrite": {
      "command": "/path/to/rag-ferrite",
      "env": {
        "LLM_API_KEY": "...",
        "EMBEDDING_API_KEY": "..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Performance

- Single binary, no Docker, no GPU required
- SQLite file-based storage (backup = `cp`)
- HNSW index persisted to disk, lazy-loaded per collection
- Query cache with 300s TTL
- Batch embedding (configurable batch size)
- Concurrent LLM calls (configurable max)

## Comparison with alternatives

| Feature | rag-ferrite | ClawRAG | mcp-rag-server | RAGent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Binary size | 15 MB | 8 GB+ (Docker) | Node.js | Node.js CLI |
| Language | Rust | Python | TypeScript | TypeScript |
| Database | SQLite | ChromaDB | SQLite | In-memory |
| Hybrid search | BM25 + HNSW + RRF | BM25 + vector + RRF | Vector only | BM25 + vector |
| MCP support | Native | Native | Native | No |
| Relevance scoring | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Contextual retrieval | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Auto-tagging | LLM (ingestion) | No | No | No |
| Query expansion | LLM (multi-query) | No | No | No |
| Corrective RAG | Auto reformulate | No | No | No |
| LLM reranking | LLM + Cohere | No | No | No |
| Install | `curl \| bash` | Docker Compose | npm install | npm install |
| Dependencies | Zero | Docker, Python, ChromaDB | Node.js | Node.js |

## Acknowledgements

The ingestion pipeline was heavily inspired by [Jonas Roman's video on production RAG workflows](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=phZ_iqu1gN0) — specifically contextual retrieval, pre-ingestion quality checks, post-chunking verification, query expansion, LLM reranking, and golden dataset benchmarking.
